approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Rock metrics are a useful capture layer for dashboard history because they can run off-hours, store repeatable values, and support later visualization without repeatedly recalculating expensive operational queries.

notes: Read-only SQL verified Metric, MetricValue, and Schedule columns that support scheduled metric capture and later dashboard visualization.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: For dashboard speed, expensive journey analytics can be calculated into a persisted dataset on a schedule rather than recalculating all historical engagement data on each page load.

notes: Read-only SQL verified PersistedDataset exists with refresh interval, schedule, result data, cache, Lava command, and build script columns.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Grouping sets can simplify Rock SQL reports that need multiple aggregation levels, such as detail totals plus higher-level rollups, without maintaining separate queries for each level.

notes: Read-only SQL executed a bounded GROUPING SETS query against FinancialAccount, verifying multiple aggregation levels in one query surface.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Rock records each Report's run duration, execution count, and most recent run date, giving administrators evidence for identifying slow or unused reports.

The v19 Unsubscribe Report can show recipient, send and unsubscribe timing, communication type or topic, and sender. Use it to investigate patterns and coach senders rather than assuming every unsubscribe has one cause.

source_refs.title: New Features & Enhancements Coming to v19

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Data Views should be treated as reusable record-set definitions: they answer which records qualify before a Report, Dynamic Report block, workflow, or other consumer decides how to display or act on those records.

notes: Read-only SQL verified DataView/DataViewFilter and Report/ReportField surfaces, including Report.DataViewId, supporting the reusable record-set distinction.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Rock v19 materializes recurring iCal schedule occurrences into ScheduleDate rows so date-based SQL and Lava queries can avoid repeatedly expanding recurrence rules. Use the generated dates rather than inventing a separate recurrence expansion process.

source_refs.title: 3 Underrated Features Churches Are Overlooking | Ep 217

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Report security controls who can view a report, while entity-appropriate grid actions can use its results for operations such as communication or export.
Because grouping sets are a SQL-level technique, public KB guidance should route users to validation against the local schema and SQL dialect before copying a community pattern into production.

notes: Read-only SQL executed a bounded GROUPING SETS query against FinancialAccount, verifying the SQL dialect feature and reinforcing local schema validation before reuse.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: In a Lava Entity command, parameter values such as `where` must be wrapped in single quotes; when `id` is also supplied, Rock ignores `where`, `dataview`, and `dynamicparameters`.

Rock v19 materializes recurring iCal schedule occurrences into ScheduleDate rows so date-based SQL and Lava queries can avoid repeatedly expanding recurrence rules. Use the generated dates rather than inventing a separate recurrence expansion process.

source_refs.title: 3 Underrated Features Churches Are Overlooking | Ep 217

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Data Integrity work should be repeatable: identify the record population, define the correction rule, test with known examples, and document the owner before making bulk changes.

Rock v19 adds a contains parameter to the Lava where filter for partial field matching rather than only equality comparisons. Confirm case, type and performance behavior with current Lava documentation before using it in broad queries.

source_refs.title: New Features & Enhancements Coming to v19

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: A field included in a Rock Report can be hidden from the on-screen grid while remaining available in the report's Excel export, which supports supplemental export-only data without cluttering the interactive view.
Before using a pivot pattern, confirm the report audience needs side-by-side category comparison; if the categories are unstable or too numerous, a normal grouped result may be easier to maintain.

The Dynamic Report block renders a selected Report and can expose chosen filters from its underlying Data View, allowing one report definition to accept viewer-controlled criteria instead of duplicating a report per campus or similar dimension.
When embedding Power BI or similar reports in Rock, pair report pages with appropriate Rock security roles and licensing checks so only authorized, licensed users can access the embedded dashboards.

notes: Read-only SQL verified report pages/blocks and Auth rows exist for Rock-side security review of embedded BI surfaces.
This does not verify external BI licensing.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: The summit's SQL-based Lava examples were intentionally simplified teaching examples. Production tools should prefer cache objects or entity commands when appropriate, return only needed fields, enforce authorization and consider business logic and query cost before choosing SQL.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Window functions are useful in Rock SQL reporting when each detail row needs aggregate context, such as total transaction amount, detail count, or percent-of-gift alongside the original transaction-detail row.

notes: Read-only SQL executed a bounded query using SUM(...) OVER (PARTITION BY TransactionId) against FinancialTransactionDetail, verifying row-preserving aggregate context in the connected Rock SQL Server.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Data View Overview strengthens the reporting guide by reinforcing Data Views as reusable qualifying-record definitions whose filters, persistence, and consumers must be checked before edits.

notes: Read-only SQL verified Data Views as reusable entity/filter definitions with persistence columns and report consumer links.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Rock's BI analytics tables are populated only when the Process BI Analytics job runs, so the shipped job must be scheduled and run at least once before BI reports can contain data.
Data integrity work should start from the exact entity and field being corrected, then identify the owner, source of truth, duplicate risk, and reporting impact before changing records.

notes: Read-only SQL verified entity/field, attribute value, DataView, Report, and person-alias surfaces used to trace source of truth and reporting impact before data corrections.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Rock distinguishes a registration from its registrants: one registration can contain multiple registrants, while account, fee, and payment information is managed separately. Reports should choose the intended grain explicitly.
People and reporting guides should distinguish cleanup, merge, verification, and governance tasks because each has different audit and permission requirements.

notes: Read-only SQL verified people, reporting, and Auth surfaces needed to separate cleanup, merge, verification, governance, audit, and permission review.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Treat community pivot examples as patterns to adapt, not final production SQL, because Rock field names, entity relationships, and reporting requirements vary by instance.

Rock v19 Connections navigation can expose list, board, grid and operational snapshot views with active, unassigned, due-soon and overdue metrics. Which views appear is configured on the connection type.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Rock's analytics-enabled tables can be used as a snapshot layer for engagement-style metrics, allowing external reporting tools to query daily counts or trends without repeatedly reconstructing every operational detail.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Rock communication lists are groups of a specific type; membership can be managed manually or synchronized from data views, so recipient troubleshooting should inspect the underlying group and its sync configuration.

Before changing a Data View, identify its entity type, filter tree, category, persistence behavior, and downstream consumers so a reporting fix does not break reports, syncs, or automations.

notes: Read-only SQL verified DataView entity/category/filter/persistence columns and Report.DataViewId/ReportField downstream consumer surfaces.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Dynamic Report filter settings separately control whether a filter is visible, whether its criteria can be edited, and whether the filter can be toggled off; supported filters can also be initialized through URL parameters.
Use OVER with PARTITION BY as a row-preserving alternative to GROUP BY when a report needs grouped calculations without collapsing the result set.

notes: Read-only SQL executed a bounded OVER/PARTITION BY query against FinancialTransactionDetail, verifying grouped calculations without collapsing detail rows.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Data Integrity adds operational guidance for cleanup and reporting quality: define correction rules, test known examples, and document ownership before data changes.

notes: Read-only SQL verified population/filter, reporting, and attribute/value surfaces used to define and test data-integrity correction rules.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Ranking window functions such as row number, rank, dense rank, and n-tile can add ordering, per-person sequence, or bucket analysis to Rock reports without procedural post-processing.

notes: Read-only SQL executed ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...) against FinancialTransactionDetail, verifying ranking/window-function support in the connected Rock SQL Server.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Provider event data should be summarized into operational reports that help staff understand delivery health without exposing unnecessary raw event detail.

notes: Read-only SQL verified communication, recipient status/delivery/open/spam fields, and reporting surfaces that can summarize provider event health without exposing raw details.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: For reporting agents, data integrity issues should be surfaced as source-data problems, not hidden by report logic that masks duplicates, missing values, or stale attributes.

notes: Read-only SQL verified source-data and reporting surfaces needed to distinguish data integrity problems from report logic.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Administrators can use multiple Process BI Analytics job instances with different enabled processes and schedules when some BI domains need more frequent refreshes than others.
Data Integrity adds guidance for people and reporting work: prove the source of truth, understand cleanup ownership, and verify downstream reporting impact before changing records.

notes: Read-only SQL verified reporting and source-data surfaces needed to prove source of truth and downstream reporting impact before people/data changes.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Email delivery and engagement events are more useful when they are tied back to the Rock communication record or person context that generated the message.

notes: Read-only SQL verified communication recipient delivery/open/spam/unsubscribe fields and person-alias linkage for tying provider engagement events back to Rock communication context.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Pivot-style SQL patterns help Rock reports turn repeated row values into comparison columns when staff need a cross-tab view rather than a long list of records.
